01-074feecf.text: This is a real tank, measured with a stereo camera. And this is a dream of it, made by a video model from one photograph.

02-ea2ed181.text: The real side isn't a recording. It's the tank rebuilt from stereo, and seen again from wherever the dream's camera goes.

03-b8ffee56.text: Grey is where no real camera ever looked. There, nothing can be checked, and the page says so.

04-a4a75e42.text: The heat shows where the dream's tank disagrees with the real one. Orange is too near. Blue is too far.

05-fa2c680c.text: The scrubber is the score. A D of one is no worse than measuring the real tank. At three, the tank has changed shape.

07-26e82050.text: Across thirty-five clips, three leave the tank for good. And the dreams don't fill the tank. They open it up.

08-f26ea6d9.text: If video models are going to make worlds, test them against a measured place, frame by frame, and say where you can no longer check.

06-0f582ec8.text: Here, just under four seconds in, the far wall opens into a corridor that isn't there. Every pixel is still checkable. Only the depth gives it away.
